notes:
Account snapshot: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics + in-app guidance). Looking to replace a homegrown embedding + search layer with a managed inference path. Short context: started with Hosted API trial in Nov 2025, moved to a 3-week POC in Jan. POC focused on conversation assistant + semantic search for help center and product UX tips.

Timeline / recent activities:
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (Jordan) — demo hosted API features, discussed perf targets (p95 latency < 120ms for short chat flows).
- 2026-01-05: POC kickoff — seed dataset (50k docs), embedding integration into Weaviate, initial cost/throughput profiling.
- 2026-01-28: POC check-in (Priya) — saw embedding latency ~40ms, generation tail occasional spikes ~350ms under burst. Documented token usage ~1.2M tokens/day projected for 150k MAU.
- 2026-02-18: Demo w/ leadership (ff_20260218_inkwell_poc_demo) — presented Dedicated sizing options; discussed reserved capacity vs hybrid burst.
- 2026-02-25: Security questionnaire returned (60% complete). Asked for SOC2 Type II and pen test summary.
- 2026-03-03: Pricing follow-up (Jordan + Finance) — team prefers committed capacity for unit economics; requesting tiered pricing with 6-month ramp credit.
- 2026-03-08: Legal kickoff — Inkwell legal sent initial redlines to MSA and DPA (see linked_drive_docs).

POC results / technical notes:
- Workload: mixed traffic — conversational chat (60%), embeddings for search (30%), occasional reranking/summary (10%).
- Perf targets: p95 latency chat <120ms, bulk embed throughput 200 req/s, tail jitter under 50ms after warm-up.
- Model preference: open/quantized Llama-family preferred; acceptable fallback to Redwood-verified smaller model for low-cost tiers. Need ability to pin model versions per route.
- Routing: want region-aware routing (NA primary, EU for EU users later). Require automated fallback to cheaper variants if capacity constrained.
- Caching: care about prefix caching for common prompts. Interest in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.

Procurement / legal specifics (current asks):
- MSA redlines: limit vendor liability cap tied to fees (client requests 12 months of fees cap), stricter IP indemnity — they want explicit carveout for customer prompts and generated output.
- DPA redlines: data deletion timelines (30 days post-termination), subprocessor list and notification, data residency clause for EU customers.
- SLA: target 99.9% availability, RTR/RTT for incident response: 1 hour P1, 24 hour permanent fix window is too long for them — asking for 72-hour RTO with interim mitigations.
- Security onboarding: require SOC2, ISO27001 spec if available, vulnerability scan results, and KMS/HSM integration for keys.

Commercial / pricing notes:
- Estimated committed spend: $10-25k/month first 6 months, growing to $40-70k/month by year 1 with feature rollout.
- Asking for 6-month ramp credit or blended rate first quarter. Finance will only sign if committed ARR inside $120k-$300k band and cancellation terms are reasonable.
- Preference for Dedicated with burst to Hosted for peak events.

Operational / onboarding notes:
- Vendor onboarding will require Redwood to fill security intake (allocated to Diego Silva) and provide SOC2 + pen test doc.
- Procurement wants a single SOW attachment to the MSA listing committed GPU SKUs and expected throughput.
- IT ops will test VPC peering and private endpoints during onboarding — internal infra ticket created (INF-1287).

Quotes / stickiness indicators:
- "Latency and predictable cost are the two gating factors for us" — VP Eng during 2/18 demo.
- Product leads liked the rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) and token-level cost breakdown in Console.

Next actions (owner Jordan):
- Circulate redline summary to legal (Jordan) and request Redwood legal's position on indemnity/cap within 3 business days.
- Schedule procurement + finance deep-dive for pricing (target 2026-03-15).
- Arrange vendor onboarding kickoff once MSA terms agreed — tentative week of 2026-03-22.

Short open questions for Redwood legal/ops:
- Will Redwood accept a 12-month fees cap or propose alternative (2x fees)?
- Can DPA include explicit 30-day deletion for non-EU data and 90-day for EU data?
- Any flexibility on SLA credits for brief, customer-impacting incidents?

CRM notes tone: choppy bullets, client responsive, legal is the current showstopper. Finance wants a firm blended first-quarter rate before procurement signs.
